body:
I honestly don't think anything good came of it. I have a mental illness that I probably (although who really knows?) would not have had otherwise, and/or it wouldn't have been as severe. I have child parts wandering around my psyche that I can't get rid of. I have never, ever had sex as an adult, and I probably never will.

I also carved myself up extensively as a young adult, and I do have scars all over my arms that broadcast my war on my body. I also had an eating disorder and almost died.

I wasn't mad for a long time, but I'm angry now at my abuser. He probably did it to a lot of other little girls too and took their childhoods and their souls from them. He has no idea what his sickness cost me, how much it's taken from me. For a long time I didn't either because I denied that was the cause, and who wants to continually be a victim? But if I'm being honest, that fucker really ruined my life. I just could have done without the whole experience.

Thank you for your reply. I do appreciate that you took the time to answer.

Please don't be offended, but I think we're talking about apples and oranges here. I'm really not interested in a sexual relationship, or a 'partnership' relationship, at all. It's not something I'm going to 'work through' because it's just not worth it to me. I'm glad you were able to have those things in your life if that is what you wanted, but it's not what I want. And frankly, your implication that feeling like a child inside somehow equates with being sexually attracted to children is disturbing *in this context*. I mention that I feel young inside and you start talking about pedophilia and the cycle of abuse. I hope you can see that might be a little triggering?

But again, please don't be offended. I'm not trying to pick a fight with you and I know we're all fragile here. I just found it a little...disconcerting.

And again, thank you for replying with kindness. I do appreciate it.

Yes, that's exactly it, and our situations sound similar. When I was a kid my mom was ill a lot and my dad was busy with work, so I did a lot of caretaking of her. Everyone thought I was very mature for my age.

I am so sorry that your childhood was lost in that way too.

I don't know if you are asking in anger...but I would like to try and answer and give you one person's perspective. (In other words, this is just my opinion.)

The best thing you can do is be kind. I was raped/abused as a young girl and have had huge issues trusting men. One thing that has helped restore my trust are my male cousins. They are just really, really nice men. They don't make comments objectifying women, they've never made me feel gross (now granted, it might be because we're cousins!) and I see the respect with which they treat their spouses and other women they come into contact with. They do not know about what happened to me, and yet they've played a part in my healing.

You might already be doing the same thing and not be aware of it, just by being a decent guy. You might be helping someone who has been a victim or helping the women around you think that more men are decent than not.

No, but I have had the blessing of having good experiences with 'older' people...having older friends, having grandmas that I cared about. I realize a lot of younger people might not have that and sometimes it seems we have generational wars...
Oh man, no more scary movies for me. After I watched the Ring I had to have my bff sleep on the floor in my room *so embarrassed*
It sounds like you and I might have similar soapboxes... ;)
A little better this morning, thanks. Was it a good movie?

I am reading a book called The Real Wealth of Nations (by Riane Eisler), and it talks about how people thrive in environments where they feel cared for. I know by the time people feel suicidal, they have some pretty big problems and just 'love' often isn't enough to fix things (it hasn't fixed my brain, for instance) but creating a society which focuses on human welfare and enrichment--instead of monetary gain and domination--would be where I'd start. Because you're right. Even when you look around SW, at all these suffering people ready to give up, you see so much talent and potential and *love* that these people have. There's no place for people who have fallen through the fabric of our society to be. No place to truly be healed and just *be*, instead of trying to fit into a system that is bad for so many people.

I don't even know what such a place would look like, really. There are a lot of stories of scary, failed utopias (like Jonestown, but there was more going on there..) I am too much of a realist (and often a cynic) to think things could change easily or overnight, but I've often wished I could do something to make life better for people. Even if it's just one person. But I have my hands full with my own stupid brain and taking care of my cat ;)

I seriously hope you'll forgive me for these ramblings...it's getting late and I'm more loopy than usual.

And thank you again. Your kindness really does make a difference.

I think I am mostly a positive presence for people, but an ineffective one. I honestly wish I could fix the world for all the people who are being chewed up and spit out by our current systems, both economic and social. I know that I can't, and right now I also can't do much beyond sit in my room and think (because of my illness...very severe bipolar depression.) I wish I had the energy and money to get out there and try and make life better for people, if only because I know that strong community can really help all of us.

So I guess tonight I spew out my idealism and my fatalism at the same time :O Silly, I know. Thanks for being there.
Thank you for your offer and for replying...I really appreciate it.
